chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: A Tunisian friend becomes foreign minister; learning Arabic
summary: The man he hid became Tunisia's foreign minister; Butler visited the mosque, learned Arabic, ate couscous with them and was nicknamed 'ram's head' when his son was born.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Took me down, place on Dunkirk, and I met all the friends. 'You look like one of us, man. I said, 'My people' They are Negro-Indian people said, 'Yeah, but you're black, and do you know it?' I said,

I generally know what's happening, yes. He says, well, do you know we're going to be all right, soon. Then everyday would say, why don't you come and visit us. Took me to the mosque. Said, I want you to learn the Arabic. See, this happened to me all the time.

He said, I'm going to send you to Egypt and you go to school and learn that, we're going to get straight. And then the next day he said, no more of that, because we're going to be going ahead, we're going to be doing something to him. I said (Inaudible). He said, we're going to send you to Transjordan. And then about two weeks later they killed King Abdullah. He said, no, you'd better wait. I said, yeah, I'm going to wait.

And then, I remember it was one Tuesday night. The paper said that Tunisia is at liberty. And this man come in and (inaudible) in France you've got -- cars can go in the middle of the street, and you've got a street in the middle, too. And cars can park on the sidewalk (inaudible) got an island. With that island, you park your car. And we sit on them benches and this man cried. He cried (inaudible). And he went to Tunisia and became the minister of state of foreign affairs. And he used to write me often. I was invited there but I never pursued this thing. Had I been there, he says then, he fell out of favor and I think I read something about -- heard something about they him or something.
And all these things -- and I used to go in the Arab

I used to speak good Arabic. Quarter, I used to be good at it. And we'd eat cous-cous and talk, hang out and do everything. (Inaudible) and when one of my sons was born, they all of them went down to see him, they were down there before me. To see if he was my son. They said, veah, call him 'muzu', That means ram's head.
